shorts.title: Trump cancels his own deposition: "matters of national importance" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Trump sued the BBC. Then he skipped court.
shorts.narration: [serious] Friends, Donald Trump sued the BBC for ten billion dollars. [beat] Then his lawyers told the court he is, quote, "no longer available for his deposition on October 16 due to other matters of national importance." [amused] That's the plaintiff. In his own lawsuit. [beat] The BBC's lawyer says that with two months of discovery left, they still haven't been able to depose him. [deadpan] The BBC says it was told: no availability whatsoever. Discovery closes December 18th. The Constitution says a president must, quote, "take Care that the Laws be faithfully executed." It doesn't say show up only when you're the defendant. [sarcastic] Ten billion dollars of confidence, zero minutes of testimony. [beat] If you're so sure you were defamed, sir, what exactly is the national emergency that beats telling a judge? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: Trump filed a $10 billion defamation and deceptive trade practices lawsuit against the BBC; BBC lawyers led by Charles Tobin asked a Florida federal court to compel Trump to sit for a deposition.
On Sept. 28 Trump's counsel said the president was 'no longer available for his deposition on October 16 due to other matters of national importance.'
Discovery closes Dec. 18, 2026; the BBC says Trump offered no availability before then and proposed January 2027 instead.
Article II, Section 3 of the Constitution says the President shall 'take Care that the Laws be faithfully executed.'

shorts.title: White House to Politico: retract or face "consequences" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Friends, the White House counsel just sent Politico a letter. [beat] Forty-eight hours to retract and apologize, or else. The letter calls the stories, quote, "demonstrably false and defamatory." [incredulous] The stories? Reports that Trump was weighing replacing his own chief of staff, Susie Wiles. [beat] Trump's response at the time? "TOTAL FAKE NEWS." [deadpan] And if Politico says no, the letter promises, quote, "an immediate review of Politico's relationship with the White House." [beat] Which is a bold threat toward an outlet Trump says was "kicked out of the White House." The First Amendment says Congress shall make no law, quote, "abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press." [sarcastic] Nobody told the founders about strongly worded letters. [beat] If the story's false, why not just prove it? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: White House counsel William Scharf sent Politico a letter giving it 48 hours to retract, apologize and remove articles about Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, calling them 'demonstrably false and defamatory'.
The letter threatens 'an immediate review of Politico's relationship with the White House' and consideration of 'appropriate and available legal remedies'.
Politico reported Oct. 15 that Trump was calling allies for advice on replacing Wiles; Trump called the report 'TOTAL FAKE NEWS' and said the outlet was 'kicked out of the White House'.
The First Amendment bars Congress from 'abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press'.

shorts.title: Supreme Court refuses Trump's prison policy; Alito, Thomas dissent #Shorts
shorts.hook: Supreme Court hands Trump a rare loss.
shorts.narration: [serious] Friends, the Supreme Court just handed the Trump administration a loss on transgender inmates' medical care. [beat] The justices refused to let the administration immediately enforce new restrictions, leaving a lower-court block in place. Only Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas would have let the policy go ahead. [deadpan] That's the whole dissent roster. [beat] The judge who blocked the policy, Royce Lamberth, is a Reagan nominee. [amused] Reagan! The administration just got out-conservatived by Reagan's pick. [beat] The policy would end surgeries, taper hormones, and cut things like makeup and wigs. About six hundred inmates were on hormone therapy in 2025. The Eighth Amendment bars, quote, "cruel and unusual punishments inflicted." [sarcastic] A fine line to walk. [beat] Should Washington dictate prison medicine? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe for the daily news, from Dylan Avanti on the Left Coast.

claims.text: On Oct. 21, 2026 the Supreme Court refused to let the Trump administration immediately enforce new medical restrictions for transgender people in federal prison, leaving a lower-court block in place; Justices Alito and Thomas would have allowed enforcement.
U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth, a Reagan nominee, ordered treatments to continue.
The policy would stop surgeries, taper hormones and end accommodations such as makeup and wigs; about 600 inmates received hormone therapy in 2025 per agency court records.
The Eighth Amendment bars 'cruel and unusual punishments inflicted'.
